summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with multiple myeloma, COPD, CAD, and a history of recent pneumonia and neck pain, was readmitted after his daughter noticed erythema and a healed ulcer on his right great toe. He denied pain or fever. He was admitted for IV antibiotics due to risk of infection from immunocompromise and prior gangrene. He received IV vancomycin, and podiatry performed a debridement, finding no deep infection. A foot X-ray showed no osteomyelitis. He was found to be dehydrated with acute kidney injury, improved with IV fluids. Anemia was managed with one unit of PRBCs. Levofloxacin was discontinued due to drowsiness and myoclonus, with transition to cefpodoxime and azithromycin for pneumonia. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotics. He was discharged home with home infusion, improved cellulitis, and stable vital signs.
